Thinking on by default; enable_thinking=false appends '<think></think>'; past assistant turns re-render reasoning only from message.reasoning_content; vLLM mimo parser defaults enable_thinking True; --default-chat-template-kwargs exists in v0.33.0
verdicts.correction: Strictly, the official template does not open <think> in the generation prompt (it ends at 'assistant\n'). That the model opens <think> itself is inferred. The ggml-org patch pre-fills '<think>\n' 'to establish the reasoning boundary', which suggests the unpatched behaviour was not reliable. vllm/parser/mimo.py:30-31 reads chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking with default True (confirmed). generation_config: temp 0.6, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, eos [248046, 248044].

verdicts.claim: Tool calling supported in compact XML form <tool_call><function=NAME><parameter=ARG>v</parameter></function></tool_call>; vLLM parser 'mimo' is the right choice
verdicts.correction: Contested. The official template renders <parameter=> only when history arguments are a dict. When arguments is a string (the OpenAI wire format) it emits the raw string, so the result is <function=NAME>{json}</function>. The ggml-org patched template header (also gist d8f56cd6..., 2026-09-22) says: 'Serialize object arguments as JSON, matching the upstream string-argument path and observed native output.' That implies the model was observed to emit JSON bodies, not <parameter=> tags. The vLLM v0.33.0 MiMoToolParser (rust/src/parser/src/tool/mimo.rs) is the Qwen3-Coder <parameter=> grammar with trim_parameter_newlines=false, and its tests cover only <parameter=> forms. If the model emits JSON bodies, vLLM's mimo parser may return empty or failed arguments. This needs an end-to-end test before 'mimo' is called dependable. The template diff against Flash-MOPD differs only in the {% generation %} lines (confirmed). The recipe parser args (--tool-call-parser mimo --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mimo, min_vllm_version 0.31.0) are confirmed.

summary: The identity and capability facts hold. The vendor's own arXiv report (2610.11959, submitted 2026-10-08) links this exact repo, the HF createdAt is 2026-09-21, and the license tag is MIT. The params (9,409,813,744; 18.82 GB, vision included, 0 MTP tensors), the config architecture, the 262,144 context, the thinking toggle, the vLLM v0.33.0 source line references, the llama.cpp fix chain and every benchmark value (report Table 6) were all reproduced. One factual correction: the 9B card does not cite the arXiv ID. It cites the report through the Pro-RL HF URL. Main contested item: the ggml-org patched template header (and gist d8f56cd6) says MiMo's 'observed native output' puts JSON arguments inside <function=NAME>, and the official template emits raw JSON when history arguments are strings. vLLM's 'mimo' parser handles only the <parameter=> XML form, so 'mimo parser is dependable for tool calls' is unverified and needs an end-to-end test. Minor points: 'harness not disclosed' is partly wrong, since Table 7 gives per-harness SWE scores, including claude code 61.7 and codex 58.5. All scores and baselines are self-reported. prithivMLmods FP8 is license:other. The Ollama page shows two pull counts (93.3K and 187.1K). Working files are in $SCRATCH/fc9b/.
